title: US-001 — Register Organization
body:
﻿## User Story
As a new organization administrator,
I want to create my organization and administrator account,
so that I can begin using JoeKnock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] User can provide:
  - Organization name
  - First name
  - Last name
  - Email
  - Password
- [ ] A new organization is created.
- [ ] Organization settings are created and initialized per finalized MVP contract:
  - `rep_visibility` defaults to `own`
  - `timezone` is required
  - `timezone` is initialized according to the finalized organization timezone contract
- [ ] A new administrator user is created.
- [ ] The user is associated with the new organization.
- [ ] The user's role is set to administrator.
- [ ] The password is securely hashed.
- [ ] The API returns authentication information after successful registration.
- [ ] Duplicate email registration within the same organization is rejected according to finalized schema/API rules.
- [ ] The same email address may exist in different organizations.
- [ ] Invalid registration data returns a useful validation error.

## Technical Notes
- Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers.
- Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup.
- Use the documented MVP schema and preserve historical references instead of hard-deleting records.

## Related database tables
- organizations
- organization_settings
- users

## Related API endpoints
- POST /api/auth/register

## Related ADRs
- ADR-004: PostgreSQL Relational Database
- Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules.
- [ ] Persistence changes align with the documented MVP schema and preserve historical integrity.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-002 — Log In
body: ## User Story  As a JoeKnock user, I want to securely log into my account, so that I can access my organization's data.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can enter email and password. - [ ] Valid credentials authenticate successfully. - [ ] Invalid credentials are rejected. - [ ] Inactive users cannot log in. - [ ] A valid JWT is returned after successful authentication. - [ ] The authenticated user's organization is available through the authentication context. - [ ] The application stores authentication information appropriately on the client.  ## Technical Notes  - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup.  ## Related database tables  - users - organizations  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/auth/login  ## Related ADRs  - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

body: ## User Story  As a JoeKnock user, I want to log out, so that my account cannot be accessed from the current session.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can log out from the application. - [ ] Client authentication information is removed. - [ ] Protected pages cannot be accessed after logout. - [ ] The user is returned to the login screen.  ## Technical Notes  - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup.  ## Related database tables  - None required for stateless JWT logout in MVP  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/auth/logout  ## Related ADRs  - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-006 — Create User
body:
﻿## User Story
As an administrator or manager,
I want to create users within my organization,
so that representatives can use JoeKnock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Authorized users can create a new user.
- [ ] User must belong to the authenticated user's organization.
- [ ] User must have:
  - First name
  - Last name
  - Email
  - Password
  - Role
- [ ] Duplicate email creation is rejected within the same organization.
- [ ] The same email address may exist in different organizations.
- [ ] Password is securely hashed.
- [ ] New users are active by default.
- [ ] Organization ID is determined by the authenticated user rather than trusted from the request.

## Technical Notes
- Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers.
- Use the documented MVP schema and preserve historical references instead of hard-deleting records.

## Related database tables
- users

## Related API endpoints

title: US-018 — View Map
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to see a map of the area I am canvassing, so that I can navigate properties while working in the field.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Map is displayed as the primary application experience. - [ ] Map supports panning. - [ ] Map supports zooming. - [ ] Properties can be represented as map markers. - [ ] Map works effectively on a tablet-sized display. - [ ] Map attribution is displayed appropriately.  ## Technical Notes  - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens.  ## Related database tables  - properties - interactions - statuses - users - teams - team_users  ## Related API endpoints  - GET /api/map/properties  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design - ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-021 — View Property Markers
body:
﻿## User Story
As a sales representative,
I want properties with visible current interactions to appear on the map,
so that I can quickly understand where interaction activity exists nearby.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] API returns properties within the visible map area.
- [ ] Property coordinates are available.
- [ ] If the current user can see a property's current interaction, the property displays one interaction pin.
- [ ] There is exactly one visible interaction pin per property for the current user.
- [ ] Historical interaction snapshots do not create additional pins.
- [ ] Multiple representative interaction groups at the same property still render one visible pin for that property.
- [ ] Pins include no status metadata in MVP.
- [ ] Pins include no interaction/count metadata in MVP.
- [ ] If the current user cannot see an interaction for the property, no interaction pin is displayed.
- [ ] Marker data respects organization visibility rules.
- [ ] Properties from other organizations are never displayed.

## Technical Notes
- Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers.
- Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens.
- Do not introduce map filtering behavior in this story.

## Related database tables
- properties
- interactions
- statuses
- users
- teams
- team_users

## Related API endpoints
- GET /api/map/properties

## Related ADRs
- ADR-001: Map-First Application Design
- ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions
- ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states.
- [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-023 — Identify Property from Map Location
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to select a location on the map and identify its address, so that I can record an interaction without manually entering the property address.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can select a location/property on the map. - [ ] Frontend sends selected coordinates to `POST /api/properties/resolve`. - [ ] Backend performs reverse geocoding as an internal implementation detail. - [ ] Backend receives the geocoded address and normalizes it for matching. - [ ] Backend checks for an existing property within the authenticated organization. - [ ] Existing property is returned when found. - [ ] New property is created and returned when no match exists. - [ ] Frontend does not call the geocoding provider directly. - [ ] Geocoding/provider errors are handled gracefully.  ## Technical Notes  - Use the finalized MVP property-resolution flow: coordinates -> reverse geocoding -> normalized address -> organization-scoped lookup/create -> resolved property. - The geocoder-returned address is the address JoeKnock uses in MVP. - Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude. - Preserve organization isolation for all property resolution behavior.  ## Related database tables  - properties  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/resolve  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`). - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want JoeKnock to create a property when I encounter a location that is not already in the system, so that I can record an interaction at that property.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Property resolution starts with `POST /api/properties/resolve` using representative-selected coordinates. - [ ] Backend reverse geocodes coordinates and normalizes address for matching. - [ ] Existing property is returned when found for the authenticated organization. - [ ] New property is created when no organization-scoped match exists. - [ ] Created/returned property is organization-owned based on authentication context. - [ ] Property creation does not require client-supplied organization identifiers. - [ ] Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude in MVP.  ## Technical Notes  - This story focuses on persistence/ownership outcomes of property resolution. - Property identity is backend-controlled and organization-scoped. - Geocoding remains internal; frontend interacts only with JoeKnock API.  ## Related database tables  - properties  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/resolve  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`). - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-027 — View Property
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to view property information after selecting it on the map, so that I can review its current information before recording an interaction.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Selecting a property retrieves property details. - [ ] Address information is displayed. - [ ] Current interaction state for that property is retrievable for authorized users. - [ ] User can access interaction workflow from the property view. - [ ] Property and interaction data respect organization/visibility permissions.  ## Technical Notes  - Property details and current interaction state may require both property and property-interactions endpoints. - MVP UI uses current state and does not expose a normal user-facing historical timeline.  ## Related database tables  - properties - interactions - users - statuses  ## Related API endpoints  - GET /api/properties/:id - GET /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions - ADR-015: Historical Interaction Data Is Preserved but Not User-Facing in MVP  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches documented authorization and visibility rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

title: US-028 — View Property Interactions (Current State)
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to see the current interaction state for a property, so that I know the latest authorized information before recording updates.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Property interaction endpoint returns current snapshots by default. - [ ] Multiple interaction groups can exist at one property across representatives. - [ ] Current snapshots are identifiable. - [ ] Results respect organization isolation and visibility permissions. - [ ] Normal user-facing historical snapshot timeline is not exposed in MVP.  ## Technical Notes  - This story is current-state focused to avoid overlap with deferred user-facing history work. - Historical snapshots remain preserved internally for reporting/support use.  ## Related database tables  - properties - interactions - users - statuses  ## Related API endpoints  - GET /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag - ADR-015: Historical Interaction Data Is Preserved but Not User-Facing in MVP  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches documented current-state semantics. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

title: US-029 — Record New Interaction
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to quickly record what happened when I interact with a homeowner, so that I can preserve the result of the interaction without interrupting my field workflow.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can start an interaction from a property. - [ ] User can select an organization-defined status. - [ ] User can enter notes. - [ ] User can enter available contact information. - [ ] Interaction date is recorded. - [ ] Authenticated user is recorded. - [ ] Interaction is associated with the correct property. - [ ] Interaction is associated with the user's organization. - [ ] A unique `interaction_group_id` is generated for a new interaction history. - [ ] A unique interaction snapshot ID is generated. - [ ] `initial_interaction_at` is set. - [ ] `changed_at` is set. - [ ] New snapshot is marked as current.  ## Technical Notes  - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. - Use the documented MVP schema and preserve historical references instead of hard-deleting records. - Honor immutable interaction snapshot rules; revisions create new snapshots instead of overwriting history.  ## Related database tables  - properties  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-004: PostgreSQL Relational Database - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag - ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Persistence changes align with the documented MVP schema and preserve historical integrity. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-030 — Save Interaction Draft
body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want my partially completed interaction to be protected from accidental data loss, so that a dead battery, dropped connection, or accidental interruption does not force me to start over.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Interaction form can save a local draft. - [ ] Draft is stored locally on the device. - [ ] Draft can be restored after the form is reopened. - [ ] Draft does not create a database interaction until the user saves/submits it. - [ ] Draft can be discarded intentionally. - [ ] Draft data is associated with the appropriate property.  ## Technical Notes  - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. - Draft preservation and retry behavior must avoid creating duplicate persisted interactions after interrupted submissions.  ## Related database tables  - None until submission; local draft storage should be keyed to the selected property context  ## Related API endpoints  - None; this story is local-client behavior until data is submitted.  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag - ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-031 — Update Interaction
body:
﻿## User Story
As a sales representative,
I want to update an interaction when information changes,
so that the current record reflects the latest information while preserving the original history.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] User can edit an authorized interaction.
- [ ] Interaction updates use `POST /api/interactions/:id`.
- [ ] Existing snapshot field values are not overwritten.
- [ ] New immutable snapshot is created.
- [ ] New snapshot keeps the same `interaction_group_id`.
- [ ] `initial_interaction_at` remains unchanged.
- [ ] `changed_at` is updated on the new snapshot.
- [ ] Previous snapshot is preserved and no interaction deletion occurs.
- [ ] Existing notes are copied to the new snapshot unless changed by the editor.
- [ ] Representatives can edit only their own interactions.
- [ ] Managers can edit interactions belonging to representatives on teams they manage.
- [ ] A manager may manage multiple teams.
- [ ] Admins can edit any interaction within their organization.
- [ ] Manager/admin edits do not transfer ownership.
- [ ] The interaction remains owned by the original representative.
- [ ] Visibility and edit authorization are separate checks.
- [ ] Organization isolation always applies.

## Technical Notes
- One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP.
- Returning to the same property updates existing interaction history rather than creating a new one.
- MVP exposes current/latest interaction state in normal workflows; no separate user-facing history timeline is introduced in this story.

## Related database tables
- interactions
- properties
- users
- statuses

## Related API endpoints
- POST /api/interactions/:id

## Related ADRs
- ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag
- Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] API behavior matches documented ownership and immutability rules.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

title: US-034 — Restrict Representative Visibility
body:
﻿## User Story
As an organization administrator,
I want to configure what representatives can see,
so that field information is shared according to our organization's workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria
Organization can configure:

```text
own
team
organization
```

Default:

```text
own
```

For `own`:
- [ ] Representatives can see only their own most recent/current interactions.
- [ ] Managers/admins continue to follow their role-based visibility rules.

For `team`:
- [ ] Representatives can see the most recent/current interactions where the interaction owner is on one of their teams, according to finalized team visibility rules.

For `organization`:
- [ ] Representatives, managers, and administrators can see all current/most recent interactions within their organization boundary.

Additional rules:
- [ ] Manager/admin edits do not transfer ownership.
- [ ] The original representative remains the interaction owner and retains visibility of their interaction.
- [ ] Organization boundaries always apply.

## Technical Notes
- Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers.
- Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup.
- Use canonical configuration value `own` (not `self`).

## Related database tables
- organization_settings
- users
- teams
- team_users
- properties
- interactions
- statuses

## Related API endpoints
- GET /api/organization/settings
- PATCH /api/organization/settings
- GET /api/properties
- GET /api/map/properties

## Related ADRs
- ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability
- ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag
- Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).
- ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules.
- [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup. - Use the documented MVP schema and preserve historical references instead of hard-deleting records. - Cover happy-path, validation, and authorization behavior with focused automated tests.  ## Related database tables  - organizations - organization_settings - users - teams - team_users - properties - statuses - interactions  ## Related API endpoints  - All protected endpoints  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-004: PostgreSQL Relational Database - ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`). - ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Persistence changes align with the documented MVP schema and preserve historical integrity. - [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-036 — Enforce Role Permissions
body:
﻿## User Story
As a JoeKnock organization,
I want actions restricted according to user roles,
so that representatives, managers, and administrators only perform authorized actions.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Representative
Can:
- [ ] View permitted properties/interactions according to visibility rules.
- [ ] Create interactions.
- [ ] Edit their own current interactions.
- [ ] View applicable statuses.
- [ ] Use map functionality.
- [ ] Use geocoding functionality.

Cannot:
- [ ] Edit another representative's interaction.
- [ ] Manage organization users.
- [ ] Manage teams.
- [ ] Manage organization settings.
- [ ] Manage statuses.

### Manager
Can:
- [ ] Perform representative functions.
- [ ] Manage multiple teams.
- [ ] See and edit current interactions belonging to representatives on assigned teams.
- [ ] View team activity.
- [ ] Manage teams.
- [ ] Manage statuses.
- [ ] View activity reports.

Additional manager rule:
- [ ] If a manager has no assigned teams, they can see/edit only their own interactions unless organization visibility settings grant broader visibility.
- [ ] Manager edits do not transfer ownership.

### Administrator
Can:
- [ ] Perform manager functions.
- [ ] See and edit any current interaction within their organization.
- [ ] Manage organization settings.
- [ ] Manage organization information.
- [ ] Create users.
- [ ] Deactivate users.
- [ ] Manage organization configuration.

Additional admin rule:
- [ ] Admin access is not restricted by team assignment.
- [ ] Admin edits do not transfer ownership.

### Authorization model constraints
- [ ] Visibility determines what a user can see.
- [ ] Edit authorization determines what a user can modify.
- [ ] Visibility and edit authorization are separate checks.
- [ ] Organization isolation always applies.

## Technical Notes
- Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers.
- Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup.
- Cover happy-path, validation, and authorization behavior with focused automated tests.

## Related database tables
- organizations
- organization_settings
- users
- teams
- team_users
- properties
- statuses
- interactions

## Related API endpoints
- All protected endpoints
- GET /api/reports/activity
- GET /api/users
- GET /api/teams
- GET /api/statuses

## Related ADRs
- ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability
- Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).
- ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules.
- [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.

title: US-037 — View Activity Report
body:
﻿## User Story
As a manager or administrator,
I want to view field activity over a selected date range,
so that I can understand canvassing activity and performance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Authorized users can request activity data.
- [ ] Report supports date ranges.
- [ ] Report can filter by representative.
- [ ] Report can filter by team.
- [ ] Report can filter by status.
- [ ] Stored timestamps remain UTC.
- [ ] Organization timezone is used to interpret report date ranges.
- [ ] `dateFrom` and `dateTo` are inclusive organization-local calendar dates.
- [ ] Report boundaries are converted using the organization's timezone before querying UTC timestamps.
- [ ] Knock counts follow finalized interaction-group / `initial_interaction_at` semantics.
- [ ] Returning to the same property by the same representative does not create a new knock.
- [ ] Snapshot revisions in an existing interaction group are not counted as additional knocks.
- [ ] Current/latest snapshot selection is deterministic using `changed_at DESC`, then `id DESC` when timestamps tie.
- [ ] Organization isolation and visibility rules are enforced.

## Technical Notes
- One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP.
- `initial_interaction_at` indicates first-knock eligibility for that interaction history.
- Reporting uses interaction/snapshot data; no separate activity-log table is introduced.

## Related database tables
- interactions
- properties
- users
- teams
- statuses

## Related API endpoints
- GET /api/reports/activity

## Related ADRs
- ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag
- ADR-009: Current State Is Derived From the Latest Accessible Snapshot
- Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
- [ ] Report output follows finalized knock/snapshot counting rules.
- [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want my interaction information protected when connectivity is interrupted, so that I do not lose information while working in the field.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Failed API requests are detected. - [ ] User receives an understandable error message. - [ ] Local interaction draft remains available. - [ ] User can retry submission. - [ ] Retry behavior does not create duplicate interaction outcomes. - [ ] Interaction updates use `POST /api/interactions/:id` for revisions.  ## Technical Notes  - Preserve local draft-first UX for unstable connectivity. - Retry flows must preserve immutable snapshot rules and existing interaction-group identity.  ## Related database tables  - properties - interactions - users - statuses  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions - POST /api/interactions/:id  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag - ADR-011: Interaction Visibility Is Permission-Based  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Retry/draft flows do not violate finalized interaction-group and snapshot behavior. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

title: US-046 — Establish Project Foundation Scaffold
body:
## User Story

As the JoeKnock implementation owner,
I want the approved MVP foundation scaffold in place,
so that feature issues can be implemented against a consistent, tested baseline.

## Purpose

Create the implementation scaffold required by the approved foundation specification without implementing business features.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] React + Vite frontend scaffold exists under ddd/frontend.
- [ ] Express backend scaffold exists under ddd/backend.
- [ ] PostgreSQL access is configured using pg/node-postgres.
- [ ] node-pg-migrate is configured for schema migrations.
- [ ] Environment/config modules and database configuration are established for dev/test.
- [ ] Vitest is configured for unit/integration test execution.
- [ ] Supertest is configured for API/integration HTTP testing.
- [ ] Playwright is configured for E2E testing.
- [ ] npm test runs the agreed automated test workflow.
- [ ] Basic app/server bootstrap and health startup behavior are in place.
- [ ] No business feature endpoint/UI implementation is included in this issue.

title: US-047 — Export Activity Data as CSV
body:
﻿## User Story
As a manager or administrator,
I want to export accessible activity/property data to CSV,
so that I can use JoeKnock reporting outputs in downstream tools.

## Purpose
Implement the MVP CSV export contract aligned with ADR-013 and docs/api_endpoints.md, using the same authorization and filters as reporting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement GET /api/exports/properties per API documentation.
- [ ] Export applies organization isolation and role authorization rules.
- [ ] Export applies representative visibility filtering before result selection.
- [ ] Export accepts and applies the same report filters used by activity reporting.
- [ ] Stored timestamps remain UTC.
- [ ] Organization timezone determines date-range interpretation and presentation.
- [ ] `dateFrom` and `dateTo` are inclusive organization-local calendar dates.
- [ ] Export filtering uses organization-local boundaries converted to UTC.
- [ ] Where an interaction timestamp is required in export output, use finalized `changed_at` current-snapshot semantics.
- [ ] Knock-count semantics remain aligned with finalized interaction-group / `initial_interaction_at` behavior.
- [ ] Export output includes approved MVP export fields (address, contact/homeowner name, phone, current status, representative, interaction date).
- [ ] CSV export does not expose cross-organization records.
- [ ] Automated tests validate authz/filter parity between report and export behavior.

title: US-048 — Enforce Interaction Current-Snapshot Integrity
body:
﻿## User Story
As a JoeKnock system owner,
I want interaction current-snapshot integrity enforced consistently,
so that current-state behavior and reporting remain correct as interactions are created and revised.

## Purpose
Implement and verify the cross-cutting invariant rules from ADR-008 and reporting semantics used by ADR-010.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For each `interaction_group_id`, exactly one snapshot is current (`is_current = true`).
- [ ] Historical interaction business data is immutable after snapshot creation.
- [ ] `is_current` transitions are controlled and only used to move current-state designation.
- [ ] Create and update interaction flows enforce the invariant at database/service boundaries as appropriate.
- [ ] Latest/current snapshot selection is deterministic:
  1. `changed_at DESC`
  2. `id DESC` as tie-break when `changed_at` is equal
- [ ] `initial_interaction_at` remains stable across revisions.
- [ ] `changed_at` changes for each new revision snapshot.
- [ ] Revisions do not create additional knocks.
- [ ] Interaction ownership remains with the original representative.
- [ ] Manager/admin edits do not transfer ownership.
- [ ] Automated tests verify invariant preservation across new snapshot creation and revision flows.
- [ ] Automated tests verify reporting semantics: `initial_interaction_at` drives knock eligibility and `changed_at` drives status reporting behavior.
- [ ] Automated tests verify that snapshot revisions do not inflate knock counts.
